sections.title: What are Large Language Models?
sections.body: Large Language Models, or LLMs, are advanced computer programs that understand and generate human language. They are built using a type of artificial intelligence called neural networks, which learn from vast amounts of text data. This training helps them predict what words or phrases should come next in a sentence.

sections.title: How LLMs Process Text
sections.body: LLMs break down text into smaller pieces called tokens, which can be words, subwords, or even characters. These tokens are transformed into numerical representations known as embeddings, which capture the meanings and relationships between words. This process allows LLMs to understand context and generate coherent responses.

sections.title: The Importance of Prompts
sections.body: Prompts are the questions or instructions we give to LLMs to guide their responses. The way we phrase these prompts can greatly influence the quality of the answers we receive. By carefully designing prompts, we can improve the relevance and accuracy of the information provided by the model.

sections.title: Enhancing LLM Performance
sections.body: Techniques like prompt engineering and automatic prompt generation help customize how LLMs respond. For example, Chain-of-Thought prompting encourages the model to explain its reasoning step-by-step, which can lead to better answers for complex questions. These methods aim to reduce errors and improve the reliability of the information generated.
